results.summary: This project outputs a VGA signal displaying a moving logo from a bitmap. It is based on the VGA playground template and uses the Tiny VGA pinout. Testing is performed through a cocotb Python test file. The documentation does not specify any external hardware beyond a VGA display.

This is an analog folded cascode operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with N-type input and on-chip bias. It operates from a 1.8V supply and provides a single-ended output. Testing requires applying input signals and measuring the output with an oscilloscope. The documentation is minimal, providing only basic specifications.

WobblyBits is a probabilistic computing chip containing six p-bits that fluctuate randomly, forming an Ising/Boltzmann machine. A 6x6 coupling matrix is loaded over SPI, and the network samples from the encoded probability distribution when the run pin is released. The p-bits are driven by a ring-oscillator true random number generator. The design is implemented in Verilog for the SKY130 process and fits in a 1x2 tile area.

This is an 8-bit counter with eight different counting modes. The mode is selected using three input pins, and the count value is displayed on eight LEDs. The design is implemented in Verilog and requires external LEDs for output. The documentation is very brief and does not describe the counting modes in detail.

This project is a TinyQV RISC-V SoC with a Wishbone interconnect, integrating a UART16550 and GPIO peripherals. It exposes debug signals and supports QSPI flash/RAM interfaces. The design is implemented in Verilog and occupies a 6x2 tile area. Extensive testing is performed using cocotb and gate-level simulations, and external hardware such as a USB-UART bridge and QSPI memory can be connected for bring-up.

This is a spiking pattern recognition core based on a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron that triggers an event when a target spike pattern is detected. It uses input switches to set the pattern and a signal generator to provide a 0.5Hz square wave. When the pattern matches, an output drives a MOSFET module to rotate a motor. The clock is deliberately set to 2 Hz to make internal processing observable, and the design is intended for educational demonstrations of robotic reflex responses.

Tiniest GPU V3 is a standalone GPU with a programmable pixel shader. It outputs VGA video and interfaces with QSPI flash/PSRAM and a gamepad, including support for an SNES controller. The design is implemented in Verilog and occupies a 6x4 tile area. The documentation is incomplete, with testing instructions still being updated.

This is an all-digital phase-locked loop (ADPLL) that locks an internal ring oscillator to a 32.768 kHz crystal reference, synthesizing a 16.777216 MHz output clock (x512 multiplication). It provides lock indicator and phase error outputs. The design is implemented in Verilog and requires an external 32.768 kHz crystal oscillator module. Optional testing can be done with a frequency counter or logic analyzer.

This is an interactive 1Hz stopwatch with hardware debouncing, lap memory, alarm target, and 9600-baud UART RX/TX telemetry. It uses a 10 MHz clock and includes modules for debouncing, BCD counting, alarm comparison, and UART communication. The design is implemented in Verilog and requires external hardware such as a 7-segment display, push-buttons, DIP switches, and a USB-to-TTL serial cable for full testing. It was developed as part of the V-SPACE Demo.

This is a constant-time AES S-Box implementing both SubBytes (encrypt) and InvSubBytes (decrypt) operations per FIPS 197. The input byte is looked up in the standard AES substitution table via purely combinational logic, with registered output. The design is inherently constant-time in hardware and is part of the rtlforge project, which generates formally-verified cryptographic IP from Rust specifications. It requires no external hardware and can be exhaustively verified by iterating all 256 input values.
